Reference

Requirements for author guides

This page lists every requirement with the prefix AUT. They come from the author guides (patterns, performance, compatibility, publishing, quality, accessibility, internationalisation, porting and troubleshooting) and from the pages those guides amend. The table is generated from the pages by a script, so each row repeats the sentence of its page.

Rules for ids:

  • An id is never reused and never renumbered, even when its requirement is removed.
  • A requirement that is removed stays in the table with the statement withdrawn, so that a test that cites the id can still be traced.
  • Ranges: 0nn patterns, 1nn performance and limits, 2nn compatibility, 3nn publishing, 4nn quality, 5nn accessibility, 6nn internationalisation, 7nn porting, 8nn troubleshooting and debugging.
  • A statement uses MUST for a rule a tool or test can check, SHOULD for a strong recommendation, and MAY for an allowed choice.

The column "Testable how" says what kind of check settles the requirement. Where the check is a review, no automatic test is possible.

Id Statement Page Testable how
AUT-001 A core MUST NOT call the clock itself, and a handler SHOULD read the clock once per batch and pass the value in. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-002 A debounce MUST cancel the pending timer before it arms a new one. Otherwise each change leaves a timer behind, and a busy editor reaches the limit of 64 held timers. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-003 The handler MUST compare the id of each timer-fired event with the id it stored, and ignore every other id. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-004 A debounce delay MUST be 50 ms or more, because a shorter delay is refused with invalid-argument. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-005 A plugin SHOULD keep its own send rate under the host rate, and SHOULD NOT depend on rate-limited as flow control. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-006 After rate-limited, the plugin MUST wait at least retry-after-ms before it sends the same kind of call again. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-007 Traps.* A throttle MUST take its time from monotonic-millis, because wall time can jump backwards and then now - last underflows in unsigned arithmetic. The code above uses saturating_sub for this reason. guide-patterns-cookbook Inspect the package and repository, or run ilium plugin verify
AUT-008 Data that the plugin can rebuild MUST go to the shared bucket or to /cache, never to a durable bucket, so that it does not fill the 16 MiB bucket. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-009 A cached value MUST carry its fetch time as now-unix-millis inside the stored bytes, and the reader MUST compare it with the current time. The host does not expire entries by age. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-010 When several sessions can refresh the same entry, only the caller whose lease returned true MAY refresh it. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-011 A view MUST render only the rows in the visible window plus a small margin, and MUST NOT put all rows into the tree. The ceiling is 4,096 nodes and 1,024 KiB for the whole tree. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-012 A view that hides rows behind a window MUST show how many rows exist and where the window is, for example 41 to 60 of 3,212, so that the user knows more exist. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-013 A plugin MUST NOT retry not-permitted, revoked, invalid-argument or unsupported. guide-patterns-cookbook Run the plugin with the grant refused and check the result
AUT-014 A retry loop MUST have a maximum attempt count and a growing delay. A suggested schedule is 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, up to 60 s, with at most 5 attempts. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-015 A submission whose repeat would harm the user (a notice, a sent line) MUST carry a dedup-key built from what makes the action unique, such as an id and a revision. guide-patterns-cookbook Inspect the package and repository, or run ilium plugin verify
AUT-016 A dedup-key MUST NOT be reused for different content within 10 minutes. The second submission is dropped as duplicate even though its content differs. guide-patterns-cookbook Inspect the package and repository, or run ilium plugin verify
AUT-017 A mismatch MUST fall back to defaults. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-018 State that must outlive a trap MUST be written to storage when it changes, not only in deactivate. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-019 A plugin that starts work for a changing input MUST keep a generation number, store it with the request, and discard a completion whose generation is not the current one. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-020 The handler MUST process every event of the batch in order, and MUST return before the event deadline (20 ms, 50 ms for tier 1). guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-021 After an events-dropped entry, the handler MUST rebuild its picture from a read call instead of trusting its incremental state. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-022 Work that can take longer than 10 ms MUST run as a job or a request. A handler that spends its 20 ms deadline on work traps the instance. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-023 A server side that needs data from the client MUST use a client request with an explicit timeout, and MUST handle timed-out and not-found (the client is gone). guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-024 A plugin that changes how it stores data MUST raise data_version and MUST provide a migrator export that converts the old layout, instead of reading both layouts inside activate. guide-patterns-cookbook Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-025 A migrate function MUST be idempotent and MUST write the new value of a key before it removes the old one, so that an interrupted run can start again from the same arguments. guide-patterns-cookbook Inspect the package and repository, or run ilium plugin verify
AUT-101 A plugin MUST be designed to run within the default of its tier, not within the ceiling. performance Inspect the package and repository, or run ilium plugin verify
AUT-102 A plugin SHOULD stay under half of each default budget in normal use, so that a bad input does not trap it. performance Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-103 Rebuildable data MUST NOT go into a durable bucket, as rule AUT-008 of the cookbook also requires, because it uses up the 16 MiB that user data needs. performance Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-104 A plugin that reports its own timing SHOULD read it with monotonic-millis and SHOULD NOT depend on a host tool being installed in the user's setup. performance Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-105 Timings for comparison with the targets MUST come from a release build. performance Unit test that every timing a plugin reports carries a release-build marker
AUT-110 When two pages differ, the defining page decides, and a page that cites an install code MUST use the cause that the defining page gives. reference-errors-and-limits Doc-lint check: extract every manifest.* and package.* install code cited with a cause in the pages and compare it with the code table of reference-errors-and-limits; any code whose cause differs fails the check.
AUT-111 An author MUST treat a limit as a trap and not as a warning. error codes and limits Fake host: call with a value above a stated maximum; assert the call returns the documented error or traps, and is never accepted with only a warning
AUT-201 A plugin MUST raise version for every package that it publishes, because the host refuses a second package with the same version and different content. guide-compatibility-and-upgrades Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-202 A plugin MUST NOT rename or remove any name of this table in a release that keeps the same id. To change a name, add the new name, keep the old one working, and document both. guide-compatibility-and-upgrades Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-203 The old name SHOULD keep working for at least two minor releases of the plugin before it is removed, and a removal MUST be announced in the changelog of the release that removes it. guide-compatibility-and-upgrades Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-204 The old command SHOULD be hidden from the command list and from the palette once the new one exists, but it MUST still run when a key or a script calls it. guide-compatibility-and-upgrades Inspect the package and repository, or run ilium plugin verify
AUT-205 Code that needs the new grant MUST check the call result and fall back when the call returns not-permitted. guide-compatibility-and-upgrades Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-206 A plugin MUST write the restore bytes in a layout whose first byte identifies the format, and MUST fall back to defaults when the first byte is not a format it knows, because the host delivers restore bytes only when the data_version equals that of the build that wrote them. guide-compatibility-and-upgrades Unit test on the fake host
AUT-207 Data that must survive a layout change MUST live in storage and be converted by a migrator, because restore bytes are delivered only when the data_version matches, and across versions only a migrator carries data. guide-compatibility-and-upgrades Unit test on the fake host
AUT-208 A plugin SHOULD keep its data readable by the previous release for one release, by adding keys instead of changing the meaning of old ones. A user who rolls back then loses nothing. guide-compatibility-and-upgrades Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-209 A plugin SHOULD rebuild and publish against each new minor contract version within the lifetime of the previous one, so that users never hold a plugin outside the window. guide-compatibility-and-upgrades Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-210 A published plugin MUST NOT list an unstable feature unless the plugin is for development use, because a T2 or T3 package that lists one is installable only in development mode. guide-compatibility-and-upgrades Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-211 A package that is meant for testers MUST carry a prerelease part in its version, so that it cannot be taken for a release. guide-compatibility-and-upgrades Unit test on the fake host
AUT-212 A plugin MUST declare a requires range no wider than the versions it was tested with. guide-compatibility-and-upgrades Unit test on the fake host
AUT-213 A plugin that provides a service or an extension point MUST raise the major version of the point when it changes the payload incompatibly, and MUST keep the old major working for as long as it lists the old major as supported. guide-compatibility-and-upgrades Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-214 The plugin MUST keep every name of the stable public list across its own releases. versioning Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-215 A plugin MUST NOT rely on a deactivate reason or a restore value to detect that an update happened, because upgrade is also the reason used by ilium plugin dev. lifecycle Unit test on the fake host
AUT-301 An author MUST offer the package file as the base route that needs no registry, and MAY add a registry as a second route through ilium plugin publish. guide-publishing-and-support Review of the project files and release notes
AUT-302 A release MUST pass check without errors and SHOULD pass lint --deny warnings. guide-publishing-and-support Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-303 A release package MUST be built with --release, because a package that carries debug information or source maps is larger and fails lint.debug-info-in-release. guide-publishing-and-support Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-304 A package MUST NOT contain a secret, a key or a token. The package is a file that anyone can open. guide-publishing-and-support Inspect the package and repository, or run ilium plugin verify
AUT-305 A signed package has one more rule: its id MUST start with the publisher id of the signing key and a dot, and an id that does not is refused with manifest.id-publisher. guide-publishing-and-support Inspect the package and repository, or run ilium plugin verify
AUT-306 The secret key MUST NOT be committed, packaged or printed. guide-publishing-and-support Inspect the package and repository, or run ilium plugin verify
AUT-307 A release MUST be signed after the last pack, and the signed file MUST be the file that users receive. Signing twice with the same key gives the same bytes. guide-publishing-and-support Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-308 The author SHOULD publish the full fingerprint on a channel separate from the download, such as the project page, so that a user can compare the two. guide-publishing-and-support Inspect the package and repository, or run ilium plugin verify
AUT-309 A leaked key MUST be announced to users on the same channel as the releases, with the fingerprint of the key that replaces it. guide-publishing-and-support Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-310 Release notes MUST name every new grant and every raised data_version. guide-publishing-and-support Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-311 A project SHOULD ship README.md and CHANGELOG.md, because lint.readme-missing and lint.changelog-missing report their absence. guide-publishing-and-support Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-312 Wherever the file goes, the author SHOULD name the file <id>-<version>.iliumpkg and SHOULD NOT rename it. guide-publishing-and-support Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-313 A release page MUST state that signed and unsigned third-party packages need Linux. guide-publishing-and-support Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-314 --unredacted works only for a plugin installed with ilium plugin dev, so an author MUST NOT ask a user for unredacted output from a normal install. guide-publishing-and-support Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-315 A plugin that logs MUST NOT write secrets, tokens, file contents or whole payloads to the plugin log. A log line is 16 KiB at most, so write a count or an id. guide-publishing-and-support Inspect the package and repository, or run ilium plugin verify
AUT-316 A report that cannot be reproduced SHOULD be turned into a fixture once you understand it, so that it never returns. guide-publishing-and-support Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-317 A plugin that cannot be fixed SHOULD be deprecated with a successor named, when a registry is in use. guide-publishing-and-support Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-318 An author MUST publish a way to reach them, in the README and in the package description, before the first release. guide-publishing-and-support Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-319 A version number, once published, MUST NOT be reused for different content. The registry refuses a duplicate on publish with registry.version-exists, and the host refuses it on install with package.version-reused. guide-publishing-and-support Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-320 Before every release you MUST run ilium plugin check, lint and test. tutorial-09-package-and-share Review only; the release step is tested through the release script of the tutorial
AUT-321 An author MUST put the support contact, the home page and the changelog in README.md and in the description, and MUST NOT add other metadata keys, because an unknown key is refused with manifest.unknown-key. reference-manifest Inspect the package and repository, or run ilium plugin verify
AUT-322 An author MUST keep the secret key out of the package and out of version control, and MUST announce a leaked key with the fingerprint of its replacement. security Inspect the package and repository, or run ilium plugin verify
AUT-401 A release MUST have no check error and no unsuppressed lint error. guide-quality-checklist Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-402 A release SHOULD pass ilium plugin lint --deny warnings, and every suppression SHOULD carry a reason that a reviewer can read. guide-quality-checklist Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-403 A plugin MUST NOT list an unstable feature in a release unless the plugin is for development use, because the shape of that feature can change without a major version. guide-quality-checklist Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-404 A plugin MUST request the smallest grant set that works, and every grant MUST be explained in the README with the feature that needs it. guide-quality-checklist Run the plugin with the grant refused and check the result
AUT-405 A plugin MUST handle not-permitted for every call of an optional grant and MUST keep working with a reduced feature set. guide-quality-checklist Run the plugin with the grant refused and check the result
AUT-406 A plugin SHOULD keep every measured use below 80 percent of its limit on the largest realistic data set, because the limit is a trap, not a warning. See Performance. guide-quality-checklist Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-407 A plugin MUST give every interactive widget a stable key. guide-quality-checklist Inspect the package and repository, or run ilium plugin verify
AUT-408 A plugin MUST have at least one test for activation, one for deactivation and one for each error code that its code handles. guide-quality-checklist Unit test on the fake host
AUT-409 A plugin that changes the layout of stored data MUST test the upgrade from the previous release with a storage snapshot of that release. guide-quality-checklist Unit test on the fake host
AUT-410 A plugin MUST NOT use colour as the only carrier of meaning. guide-quality-checklist Review of the rendered views at each theme and density setting
AUT-501 A plugin MUST NOT use colour as the only carrier of meaning, and MUST give every status a word or a glyph beside its colour role. accessibility-and-theming Review of the rendered views at each theme and density setting
AUT-502 A plugin MUST read reduced-motion and stop its own animating timers when it is true. accessibility-and-theming Review of the rendered views at each theme and density setting
AUT-503 A plugin MUST work in compact density at 40 columns and in both icon modes, and MUST end every icon-only control with a text label that stays when icons are not drawn. accessibility-and-theming Render test: count the rendered rows at 40 columns in compact density with each icon mode and assert that no row is cut and every icon-only control has its label; scan the tree for rgb and indexed colours and assert none
AUT-504 A plugin MUST use the nine colour roles and avoid rgb and indexed colours, because only a role follows the theme. accessibility-and-theming Render test: count the rendered rows at 40 columns in compact density with each icon mode and assert that no row is cut and every icon-only control has its label; scan the tree for rgb and indexed colours and assert none
AUT-505 A plugin SHOULD test every view at 40 columns by 12 rows, which is the size lint.widget-missing-key renders at, and SHOULD give a min constraint to a segment that must stay readable. layout Unit test on the fake host
AUT-506 A plugin SHOULD prefer fill and percentage for text segments. layout Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-507 A view MUST show state in text as well as in colour. ui-model Review of the rendered views at each theme and density setting
AUT-601 A plugin MUST NOT assume that it can learn the user's locale or time zone from the host. guide-internationalisation Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-602 A plugin MUST measure width with display-width and MUST NOT use len(), chars().count() or String.length for layout. guide-internationalisation Render a view with wide characters and combining marks on the fake host; assert each row's cell width equals the display-width of its text
AUT-603 A plugin that cuts text to fit MUST cut at a grapheme boundary, and SHOULD end a cut with …, which takes one cell. guide-internationalisation Render a view on the fake host and check row widths
AUT-604 A plugin SHOULD NOT call display-width once per character for a long text. Measure once, and cut only when the text is too wide. guide-internationalisation Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-605 A plugin SHOULD leave room for a longer label and SHOULD NOT depend on a fixed width. guide-internationalisation Render a view on the fake host and check row widths
AUT-606 A plugin MUST treat text from outside as data: it MAY contain wide characters, combining marks, text in any direction and any length. guide-internationalisation Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-607 A plugin SHOULD NOT promise correct display of right-to-left scripts, and SHOULD state this in its README if its users need them. guide-internationalisation Review of the plugin README for the statement, when the plugin targets users who need right-to-left scripts
AUT-608 A plugin that ships several languages MUST fall back to one default language for any missing message, and MUST NOT show a message id to the user. guide-internationalisation Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-609 A plugin that wants a translated settings page SHOULD keep the manifest titles in one language and put the translated text in views it draws itself. guide-internationalisation Review of the project files and release notes
AUT-610 A plugin MUST NOT translate command ids, setting keys, error codes and event names. guide-internationalisation Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-611 A plugin that shows a time MUST write the zone or say that it is relative, and MUST store times as UTC milliseconds, never as local text. guide-internationalisation Render a view on the fake host with the test clock at a known UTC time; assert the displayed text contains either the zone name (for example UTC) or a relative phrase (for example 5 min ago), and never a bare local-looking time; assert stored times are UTC milliseconds
AUT-612 A plugin SHOULD use YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss for absolute times unless the user chooses another form. guide-internationalisation Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-613 A plugin that formats time MUST be tested with the fake clock, which starts at 2030-01-01 00:00:00 UTC. guide-internationalisation Unit test on the fake host
AUT-614 A plugin SHOULD use a dot and no group separator in machine-readable output, and SHOULD use metric units for sizes it shows. guide-internationalisation Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-615 A plugin that sorts names for people SHOULD fold case and accents before comparing, and SHOULD NOT claim a language-correct order. guide-internationalisation Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-616 A plugin MUST store time as UTC milliseconds and MUST state the zone or show relative time when it displays a time. api-clock-and-timers Render a view on the fake host and check row widths
AUT-617 A plugin MUST measure text with display-width and MUST NOT size a column by character count. widgets-text Render a view on the fake host and check row widths
AUT-618 A plugin MUST pass a toast or notice body already in the language it chose, and the host MUST show it unchanged apart from escape removal and the width cut. guide-internationalisation A test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-619 The host's fixed words around a plugin's text are not in the plugin's language and a plugin MUST NOT rely on them matching its own. guide-internationalisation A test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-620 The grant reason has one value; the review dialog shows it verbatim as data, cut at the dialog width with …, never mixed into a host sentence. guide-internationalisation A test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-621 A plugin SHOULD write the grant reason in a language its users read and SHOULD keep it short enough to fit 60 cells after a translation. guide-internationalisation A test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-622 Grant ids, the plugin id and capability names in the dialog are identifiers and are never translated. guide-internationalisation A test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-701 A port SHOULD put logic about panes and agents on S and drawing on C, and SHOULD send messages between them rather than share state. guide-porting-from-other-plugin-systems Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-702 A port MUST declare every grant its calls need, and ilium plugin check reports an import without a grant as component.import-ungranted. guide-porting-from-other-plugin-systems Run ilium plugin check or lint and read the finding
AUT-703 A port that waits in a loop MUST be rewritten as events: start the work, return, and handle the result when request-completed arrives. guide-porting-from-other-plugin-systems Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-704 A port SHOULD prefer the typed primitive (terminal.read-screen) over a program, because the primitive needs a weaker grant. guide-porting-from-other-plugin-systems Read the manifest; assert it requests terminal.read-screen and no process.run grant for the same data
AUT-705 A port MUST NOT ask for a write grant wider than the folder it writes to. guide-porting-from-other-plugin-systems Read the manifest; assert each fs.write scope is the folder the plugin writes to; a scope is wider when its name is an ancestor of that folder or a wildcard over it
AUT-706 A port SHOULD be written as a new plugin with a new id, and SHOULD NOT reuse the name of the original in a way that suggests it is the same product. guide-porting-from-other-plugin-systems Compare the manifest id with the original plugin's id; assert they differ (the name rule is review only)
AUT-801 An author SHOULD turn every fixed run-time bug into a test before the next release. guide-troubleshooting Unit test on the fake host
AUT-802 An author MUST read the code in an install error before changing anything, because each code names one cause. guide-troubleshooting Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
AUT-803 A report to the host project SHOULD contain the Ilium version, the plugin id and version, the manifest, the last 100 log lines and a test that reproduces it. guide-troubleshooting Unit test on the fake host
AUT-804 A plugin MUST NOT depend on --unredacted traces to diagnose a user's problem, because that flag works only for a plugin installed with dev. debugging Review against the page, plus a test where the rule has an observable result
